ui.title: Different counsel. Your decision.
ui.help: These written perspectives share the reports below. They are not a live debate or predictions. Choose a speaker to continue with optional AI text and voice; no connection starts automatically.
ui.stale: This briefing is from turn {turn}; the campaign is now at turn {current}. Finish the current presentation to refresh it.
ui.no_season: The first seasonal council awaits a resolved campaign turn. You can still consider the selected city and each advisor’s approach.
ui.quiet: No visible Dispatch headlines were selected this season.
ui.omitted: {count} further reports are not included. Read the full Dispatch before deciding.
ui.survey: Societal report: {level} · {age} turns old. Missing or banded values remain uncertain.
ui.no_city: Select a settlement you own to bring its public reports before the council.
ui.factors_limited: Only the first {limit} factors of each reading are supplied.
ui.city_question: Which cost in this city would you accept, and which would you refuse?
ui.question: Help me weigh this council’s perspectives against the shared reports and my patron’s mandate, if any. What should I check before deciding?
ui.lucius_locked: Lucius’s seat is still unfilled. Complete the required government building to invite his governing perspective.
ui.battle: The council awaits the end of the battle view. No live campaign or economic readings are taken while the tactical worker is active.
ui.presentation: Finish the turn presentation and close its report before convening or changing a pledge.
ui.patronage_help: Choose an optional narrative patron through a completed matching temple. Zeus and Ares ask different things of a ruler. Their words shape counsel; pledges grant no new combat, income or temple bonuses.
ui.divine_source: AUTHORED DIVINE ADDRESS · ORIGINAL GAME FICTION
ui.temple_needed: You have no completed matching temple in an owned settlement. Review construction in a city that supports this patron’s existing temple chain.
ui.select_seat: Choose the temple at which you will pledge:
ui.confirm_pledge: Pledge to {name} at {city}? This replaces any current pledge and clears its progress. Unfulfilled charges are checked when a campaign season resolves; earlier honors remain fulfilled. The existing temple retains its normal effects.
ui.confirm_renounce: Renounce your current patron? Current mission progress will be cleared. Earlier fulfilled missions remain recorded. You can pledge again later.
ui.progress: Mission progress: {progress} / {target} · last checked on turn {turn}
ui.awaiting: This pledge has not yet reached its first seasonal check.
ui.fulfilled: This divine charge has been fulfilled. Your patron’s perspective remains part of the council.
ui.remembered: You have fulfilled this patron’s charge before.
ui.temple_lost: No matching temple remains under your control. Restore one before this mission can progress.
ui.pledged: Your pledge is recorded. The next seasonal council will weigh its demands.
ui.renounced: Your pledge has been released. Your next decision is your own.
ui.changed: The campaign changed before this choice could be made. Review the refreshed temple and mission details.
ui.blocked: Resolve the active battle or pending defense before changing divine patronage.
ui.finished: This campaign has ended. Its pledges can be read but no longer changed.
ui.live_help: One short turn per unlocked advisor, chaired by Marcus. This action sends a frozen visible report to ElevenLabs using up to three private connections and one question per speaker. It never repeats automatically.
ui.live_ready: Select an owned city after a resolved season, then ask to hear the council.
ui.live_needs_context: Finish the turn presentation, close Dispatch and select an owned city with a current season report.
ui.live_complete: The discussion has ended. Its snapshot may become out of date; your orders remain yours.
ui.live_stopped: Discussion stopped. No further speakers will be contacted.
ui.live_context_changed: The context changed, so the discussion stopped. Start again explicitly to use the new reports.
ui.live_timeout: The discussion reached its time limit and stopped. The written council remains available below.
ui.live_unavailable: A private advisor could not complete the discussion. No retry was made; the written council remains available below.
ui.live_too_long: A reply exceeded the discussion limit. Its text is truncated and playback has stopped.
ui.live_too_large: These reports exceed the discussion size limit. The written council remains available.
ui.live_empty: No generated discussion yet. The written perspectives below work offline.

marcus.name: Marcus
marcus.counsel: Begin with what the reports establish. Decide which obligation deserves your attention this season, then ask whether you could defend the cost to those who bear it. A larger realm is not, by itself, a better governed one.
marcus.city: Consider the city’s public order alongside its growth and income. No single favorable total absolves us from examining its causes.
marcus.season: Treat each headline as evidence of an event, not proof that your next choice will succeed. What has changed your responsibilities?

patrons.zeus: Zeus asks you to keep a city steady before reaching for another. I would ask whether the promise serves its people even when the god is no longer watching.
patrons.ares: Ares’s appetite does not settle your duty. A wider realm is a choice, and peaceful acquisition counts. Ask what you would leave neglected in pursuing it.

marcus.locked: Marcus is your companion from the beginning.

lucius.name: Lucius
lucius.counsel: A worthy intention still needs a workable administration. Identify the factor your decision would address, the people who would pay, and the report that could show whether it helped. Patience without a question can become neglect.
lucius.city: Read the age and precision of the city’s survey. If the report is incomplete, ask what you can verify before promising a remedy.
lucius.season: Which reported event exposes a recurring weakness in government? Repairing that cause may serve the realm longer than answering its loudest symptom.

patrons.zeus: A gentler tax setting must still support the work the city needs. Read the actual order factors and the age of the survey before calling calm a lasting settlement.
patrons.ares: If the borders move, the obligations move with them. Examine the treasury, administration and reported condition of new cities before treating expansion as success.

lucius.locked: Lucius’s seat is still unfilled. Complete the required government building to invite his governing perspective.

gaius.name: Gaius
gaius.counsel: A plan begins with the force you actually command, the ground you can see and the time the march will cost. Leave room for what your scouts have not established. Courage does not make a hidden army smaller.
gaius.city: Ask what defending this city would leave unavailable elsewhere. A garrison has a duty here before it becomes a promise on a distant road.
gaius.season: Which reported change has altered your readiness? Review the next order and the position it would leave your force in before committing another season.
gaius.locked: Gaius joins after a season with an owned completed tier-three barracks. Queued or foreign buildings do not count.

patrons.zeus: Zeus asks for a city that can endure. I would first ask what must remain to defend it, and whether a march would leave that duty unanswered.
patrons.ares: Ares welcomes another border, but a god will not carry your supplies. Examine the route and what you know of opposition. Peaceful acquisition can answer this mandate too.

discussion.prompt: Give your one council turn in at most three short sentences and 60 words. Speak only as council_discussion.speaker, from the frozen visible evidence. Marcus chairs by naming the central tension. Lucius weighs institutions and civic costs; Gaius weighs security and operational costs. If prior turns exist, address one of their points with a distinct priority or a reasoned disagreement. Identify uncertainty. Divine alternatives are authored choices only: never invent or execute costs, rewards or options. End with one practical consideration for the player.
